text: Agile methodology is a modern approach to project management, especially popular in software development. Instead of working on one huge final product, teams use iterative development, breaking the work into small, manageable parts called sprints. Each sprint, which usually lasts two to four weeks, focuses on completing specific features. Before a sprint begins, the team reviews a backlog, which is a prioritized list of tasks. These tasks are often written as user stories, describing a need from the customer's perspective, like "As a user, I want to log in." To track progress, the team holds short daily standups, where each member shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any obstacles. This constant feedback and adjustment allow the team to adapt quickly to changes. The main goal is to deliver value early and often, rather than waiting until everything is perfect.
